lesson.title: ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ: ਇੱਕ ਵੱਡਾ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ (Amritsar: A Major City)
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: ਤੁਸੀਂ ਦਰਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਖੇਤ ਬਾਰੇ ਸਿੱਖਿਆ। ਅੱਜ, ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇ ਇੱਕ ਵੱਡੇ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਬਾਰੇ। (You've learned about rivers and fields. Today, one of Punjab's major cities.)

New word: ਸ਼ਹਿਰ (shahir, city). ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ (Amritsar) is one of Punjab's most important cities — you already learned in an earlier grade that its name means 'pool of nectar,' and that Guru Ram Das founded the town it grew from. Write a sentence about Amritsar using the pattern: ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਇੱਕ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਹੈ (Amritsar is a city), then add one more detail you remember about it.
You now have real vocabulary connecting this week's geography to what you already know about Amritsar's history. Tomorrow you'll use everything from this week to write a persuasive piece.

objectives: Learn the word ਸ਼ਹਿਰ (city) and connect it to Amritsar as a real example
Recall and reuse prior knowledge about Amritsar's history
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's river and farmland vocabulary.
2. Introduce ਸ਼ਹਿਰ and Amritsar, connecting back to earlier Sikhi-grade content about Guru Ram Das founding it.
3. Have the child write the practice sentence plus one remembered detail.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's topic: persuasive writing.
differentiationTips: Struggling: if the child doesn't remember Amritsar's history detail, simply reintroduce it rather than requiring recall
Ready for more: ask them to name one more real or hypothetical detail about a city they'd want to include in a description
All Gurmukhi words used in this lesson were validated against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. ਸ਼ਹਿਰ = city. 2. Amritsar's name means 'pool of nectar.' 3. Guru Ram Das founded the town that became Amritsar.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Connects this week's geography vocabulary to prior Sikhi-course content (Grade 5's Guru Ram Das lesson), reinforcing cross-subject knowledge while building toward Day 4's persuasive writing.

rows.problem: Who founded the town that became Amritsar?
